newsitem.title: USA: GM touts Olympic pact as unique promotion opportunity.
newsitem.headline: GM touts Olympic pact as unique promotion opportunity.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said its sweeping media and sponsorship agreement with the U.S. Olympic Committee and NBC Inc. announced Wednesday presents the automaker with an unprecedented opportunity to showcase its car and truck brands.
The deal, announced at NBC Studio 1A in New York, designates the U.S. No. 1 automaker as the official domestic car and truck of the U.S. Olympic team through the 2008 Olympic Games.

Terms of the deal were not released. But a GM official who asked not to be named said the value could come close to $1 billion. The total would depend on such factors as how much advertising GM buys from NBC and the value of its cars that are used during the Olympics.

"The real relevance here is that this deal represents something unique to GM and its brands," Phil Guarascio, general manager of marketing and advertising for GM's North American Operations, told reporters.
"This is not about dollars, it's about value," he said.
Guarascio said GM's investment is "not necessarily new money" because the automaker has gotten more aggressive in general with its marketing spending.
He added the long-term nature allows GM enough lead time to could plan a new-vehicle launch during the 2002 Olympic Winter Games in Salt Lake City if it wanted to.

GM's contract with the USOC allows GM, its vehicle divisions, subsdiaries such as GM Goodwrench and Delphi Automotive Systems, and its new GM Certified Used Vehicles brand to use the Olympic rings and logos in all advertising and marketing activities.
During the 2002 games in Salt Lake City, GM will have on-site rights similar to its involvement in the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta.

The deal only applies to GM's U.S. operations. It does not designate GM as the sole automotive sponsor for the USOC, said John Krimsky, USOC deputy secretary general. The USOC plans to have one more car sponsor, he said.

For more than two years, GM has been taking steps to raise its corporate profile and better distinguish its vehicle lines among consumers under a strategy called "brand management." Steps include a new GM Certified Used Vehicles brand and becoming the exclusive automotive sponsor for the new Women's National Basketball Association.

Ironically, those actions come as GM has sunk to its lowest share of the U.S. market in decades -- 28.4 percent -- as it faces stiffer foreign competition and has been hurt by six labour strikes this year.

One analyst said GM's Olympic deal gives it a powerful tool to reach a large audience. But he said it may work against the brand management philosophy of targeting focused messages to specific audiences.
"The fact that it was done as such a big, giant broad-based sweep infers that's the opposite of focus," said James Hall, vice president of industry analysts at AutoPacific Inc. in Southfield, Mich.
Susan Jacobs, president of automotive consultant Jacobs and Associates, questioned whether GM's Olympic marketing investment could be better used on consistent marketing over a longer period of time.
"What your Olympic advertising does as a sponsor is bring you in front of a lot of people who may or may not put you on their shopping list," she said.

GM is the first major Olympic sponsor to commit to a long-term agreement. It marks a new approach under which the USOC and NBC, a unit of General Electric Co., work jointly to enlist corporations for both Olympic sponsorship and TV advertising.
